title: Collections in Depth
description: The Java Collections Framework beyond the basics: how lists, sets, maps, stacks and queues behave, generics and wrapper types, the operation costs that Big-O describes, the equals and hashCode contract, how HashMap uses it, choosing a collection for a need, and sorting with Comparator.
sourceCoverageNotes: Second-mate module grouping, not syllabus: calendar days F25 'Collections in depth' and F26 'HashMap, equality, sorting' form this module because both teach the collections themselves; the frozen curriculum defines no modules for this course.
Source slice: F25 rows 0-4 and F26 rows 0-3, each mapped exactly to one topic; no row is split or shared.
F25 row 3 'Reading: wrapper types and autoboxing' is the Reading topic wrapper-types-and-autoboxing.

Boundaries: lists-sets-and-maps-in-depth teaches behavior of each interface; choosing-the-right-collection teaches selecting an implementation from needs; big-o-basics owns the cost vocabulary that both use.

Planned module lab collections-in-depth/coding-lab (Java, JUnit, mvn -q -o test; about 35 minutes on F25 and 12 on F26) practises lists-sets-and-maps-in-depth, stacks-and-queues, generics, big-o-basics, the-equals-and-hashcode-contract and how-hashmap-works; it is authored in this module's PR and moduleLabs lists it once it exists.
